description: Open source repositories that are in scope for active bug bounty programs, ordered by newest stable release first.

repos.name: Shopify/cli
repos.description: MIT licensed TypeScript monorepo for the Shopify CLI, the command line toolchain partners and merchants use to scaffold, develop, preview and deploy Shopify apps, themes, Hydrogen storefronts and Functions; it ships as the @shopify/cli npm package alongside a Homebrew tap, and every version bump is cut as a tagged GitHub release. In scope for Shopify's HackerOne bug bounty program through the structured scope https://github.com/Shopify/*, a SOURCE_CODE asset whose instruction reads "Environment: Non-core. Public repositories available under the Shopify organization in Github", so coverage is org-wide rather than an enumerated repository list, and the HackerOne API reports that scope eligible_for_bounty=true and eligible_for_submission=true. The material caveats are the medium maximum severity on that scope and Shopify's scoring method: awards come from Shopify's Bug Bounty Calculator with a $500 floor for scores under 3, and for non-core properties the Environment Score modifiers are forced to Low for Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability, which deflates open source findings well below the program's headline $200,000 ceiling; a functional proof of concept showing impact on Shopify or its merchants is mandatory. Latest stable release: 4.6.1 (2026-08-07, 15:16 UTC), badged Latest by GitHub, with no same-day pre-release tags in this repository.

repos.name: trustwallet/wallet-core
repos.description: Apache-2.0 licensed cross-platform, mobile-focused C++ library implementing the low-level cryptographic wallet primitives, key derivation, address generation and transaction signing, for more than 130 blockchains including Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB, Cosmos and Solana, exposed over strict C interfaces with idiomatic Swift, Java/Kotlin, WebAssembly, npm, Go and Kotlin Multiplatform bindings; it is the cryptographic foundation of Trust Wallet and cuts a tagged GitHub release roughly weekly. In scope for Binance's Bugcrowd bug bounty program: this repository's own GitHub security policy states that TrustWallet participates in Binance's bug bounty and directs vulnerability reports to https://bugcrowd.com/binance for eligible scope and rewards, and Bugcrowd's public engagement directory lists Binance as an open, non-private Bug Bounty engagement paying $200 to $10,000 with a stated maximum of $100,000. The material caveat is verification depth: unlike HackerOne, Bugcrowd exposes no per-target bounty-eligibility flag, and the Binance brief page is JavaScript-rendered while its target_groups and .json endpoints are authenticated, so this repository's coverage rests on the first-party security policy plus the public directory rather than on a machine-readable in-scope target list. Latest stable release: 4.7.3 (2026-08-07, 14:14 UTC), badged Latest by GitHub and carrying no pre-release badge, with no same-day pre-release tags; the npm publish of @trustwallet/wallet-core 4.7.3 trailed the GitHub release by roughly an hour and a half.

repos.name: vercel/eve
repos.description: Apache-2.0 licensed TypeScript framework from Vercel for building durable, filesystem-first AI agents, replacing continuation-token session APIs with fixed ID-addressed handles and channel-local operations, and supplying delegated subagents with persistent sessions, tool definition and streaming execution, multi-channel delivery to Slack, GitHub and Linear, interactive authorization flows and pluggable sandboxes on top of the AI SDK; it publishes as the eve npm package and cuts a tagged GitHub release for nearly every patch, several times a week. In scope for the Vercel Open Source program on HackerOne, which lists https://github.com/vercel/eve as a SOURCE_CODE asset with eligible_for_bounty=true, eligible_for_submission=true and critical maximum severity, and whose instruction reads "Please assign this to any project involving the eve repo. This is considered tier 2". The material caveat is that tier placement: the policy describes Tier 2 (Standard Priority) as projects with smaller user bases, niche use cases or experimental configurations and states that bounties are awarded at a lower rate than Tier 1, though a critical or high severity finding with a clear reproducible exploit chain may be paid at Tier 1 levels case by case; every report needs a zip proof-of-concept artifact reproducible on a stable release, and canary or RC-only issues superseded by a stable version are out of scope. Latest stable release: eve@0.31.1 (2026-08-07, 12:50 UTC), badged Latest by GitHub, with no same-day pre-release tags; the package's separate beta dist-tag (0.6.0-beta.20) is a stale prerelease line and was excluded.
